key_insight: Large language models can automate reproducibility checks in the social and behavioral sciences, matching original qualitative conclusions far more often than human reanalysts.
engineering_relevance: This suggests LLM-based audit pipelines could scale reproducibility assessment workflows where manual reanalysis is too slow or costly.
method: Evaluated 76 published studies with predefined claims from the behavioral and social sciences.
Compared LLM-generated reanalyses against original findings and human reanalysis.
Measured both effect-size recovery and agreement on qualitative conclusions.
evidence_signal: The LLM pipeline recovered original effect sizes in 41% of studies within ±0.05 Cohen's d and matched qualitative conclusions in 96% of cases, versus 34% and 74% for human reanalysts.
watch_item: Some studies could not produce a viable effect-size estimate, so automated auditing still needs fallback handling and careful validation.
paper_title: Automated reproducibility assessments in the social and behavioral sciences using large language models
